transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-05-07 15:00 PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood CSM), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Bluehex VP Eng), Sam Ortiz (Bluehex DevOps), Ellen Park (Bluehex Product), Ravi Patel (Bluehex Security), Jordan Lee (Bluehex SRE)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro — I'm Maya Chen, AE for this account, Diego is our CSM, Liam is our SE who will run the perf stuff. How's everyone?
[00:12] Priya: Hey, thanks. We're excited to get the onboarding started. We've got a mix from infra, product, security on the line.
[00:18] Diego: Great. Goal for today is to align on the sprint-zero scope, access, and immediate blockers. We'll capture action items.
[00:26] Sam: One ask up front — we need to understand the network pattern. Do you support VPC peering or do we need VPN? Also any port requirements?
[00:35] Liam: We support both. For private deploys we generally do VPC peering and for hosted we use private endpoints. Ports are minimal — mostly HTTPS 443. We'll share a checklist.
[00:45] Ravi: On security side, we need SOC2, penetration test cadence, and details on KMS/HSM integrations. Any docs you can share?
[00:55] Maya: Yep, we'll send the security packet. I'll include the SOC2 excerpt, our data retention policy, and KMS integration notes.
[01:05] Ellen: For product, our main success metric for pilot is latency under 150ms p50 for short prompts and budget of $0.001 per token equivalent, roughly.
[01:15] Liam: Got it. We'll validate those targets during the perf deep-dive. Quick note — if you need lower latency often the dedicated footprint helps but costs more.
[01:25] Priya: What's the typical delta between hosted and dedicated? Ballpark numbers?
[01:32] Liam: Ballpark — hosted optimized can hit ~120-180ms for many open models at small seq; dedicated with pinned GPUs and optimized kernels can do 60-110ms depending on model and quant. But depends on batch profiles and KV cache usage.
[01:46] Jordan: You said KV cache — do you mean KV cache or KV cash? (laughs)
[01:50] (crosstalk)
[01:52] Liam: KV cache, sorry. Sometimes speech-to-text messes that up.
[01:56] Priya: Okay. For the pilot we want to try hosted first to move quick then test dedicated if we see tail latency issues.
[02:08] Diego: That aligns with our recommended pattern for many customers — quick hosted onboarding, then dedicated pilot if throughput/latency needs require.
[02:20] Sam: Regarding data residency — our legal team wants logs to not leave region. Is that possible with the hosted offering?
[02:29] Maya: We have region controls; hosted can pin to a region, but for strict residency the Private (VPC/on-prem) is the recommended route. We'll lay out options in the packet.
[02:40] Ravi: Also need audit logs and access to raw request logs for compliance. Any retention limits?
[02:48] Diego: We can provide audit logs, and retention tiers are configurable — we have an advanced observability add-on for longer retention. We'll include that pricing in the follow-up.
[03:02] Priya: Who needs to be on the technical deep-dive call? I assume SRE, DevOps, and maybe one product for acceptance criteria.
[03:10] Ellen: Yes, product will join for success criteria.
[03:14] Maya: For the perf run we'll also need some representative prompt sets and the expected traffic profile — qps distribution, seq length histogram. That helps Liam pick compile kernels and batching strategy.
[03:26] Sam: We'll export a sample of logs and prompt sets. Expect many short queries (~16-64 tokens) and some long context cases.
[03:33] Liam: Perfect. Also please include any streaming use-cases — streaming can affect batching and latency tradeoffs.
[03:40] Priya: We do have chat streaming in one feature.
[03:44] Liam: Ok, note that.
[03:46] (pause)
[04:00] Maya: Quick recap on the pilot scope — 2-week pilot in staging, measure p50/p95 latencies, cost per request, and quality regressions on prompt set. If those are good we'll plan a limited production ramp.
[04:12] Priya: Sounds reasonable. Timeline? We want staging pilot in 2 weeks. Is that achievable?
[04:17] Diego: If we get staging access within 5 business days, yes. That means network creds, sample prompts, and a contact for peering.
[04:25] Sam: We'll prioritize that.
[04:28] Maya: I'll send a runbook and the checklist after this call.
[04:32] Priya: Ongovernance — who will be Redwood's day-to-day contact?
[04:36] Maya: Diego will be your CSM and primary contact for runbook/events, Liam for SE issues, and I'm the AE.
[04:42] Jordan: Any SLA commitments for the pilot?
[04:45] Diego: Pilot doesn't have a formal SLA but we'll monitor and set up alerts. For Dedicated or Enterprise tiers, SLA options are available.
[04:56] Ravi: For the security deep-dive, who will own the artifact exchange? We prefer SFTP or secure share links.
[05:04] Maya: We'll use the secure share link and can also push docs to your secure S3 if needed.
[05:10] Ellen: Regarding cost — can you provide an estimate of monthly cost if we ramp to 10M tokens a month on hosted vs dedicated?
[05:19] Liam: We'll model that in the pricing sheet. Hosted cost tends to be per-token; dedicated is a reserved capacity number plus infra, so you'd see different amortization. We'll send sample TCO.
[05:30] Priya: Any gotchas with model versioning? We need to freeze model versions for the pilot to avoid noisy regressions.
[05:37] Diego: You can pin model versions in the platform and we support canary rollouts. We'll include a short doc on how to pin and rollback.
[05:46] Priya: Great.
[05:49] (silence)
[06:02] Maya: Ok let's move to the checklist that Liam will need for the perf run.
[06:06] Liam: Checklist — staging endpoint, example prompts, traffic profile, expected SLOs, any rate limiting in prod, and whether you want function-calling / tool-calling enabled for the pilot.
[06:18] Sam: We won't enable external tool-calls for the pilot; it's internal routing only.
[06:23] Liam: Noted. Also, if you plan to use quantized models to save cost let me know — quantization can affect quality and latency.
[06:31] Priya: We might try 4-bit quant for cheaper runs, but need quality review.
[06:36] Liam: We'll include quantization recommendations in the benchmark plan.
[06:40] Priya: Who signs off on quality regressions? Product or engineering?
[06:44] Ellen: Product will sign off on acceptance criteria; we'll work with engineering on feasibility.
[06:50] Maya: On handoff — Diego will follow up with the runbook, and Liam will schedule the perf deep-dive. I'll attach the security packet.
[07:00] Priya: Anything else on infra? Jordan: we may need ephemeral keys for the test environment; how do you rotate keys?
[07:09] Diego: We support short-lived API keys and can integrate with your KMS for rotation. We'll cover rotation docs in the packet.
[07:18] Ravi: For audit trails, can we get both access logs and per-token cost breakdown?
[07:25] Diego: Yes, the console provides token-level cost and a per-route breakdown. We'll demo that in the deep-dive.
[07:35] (10+ minutes of clarifying questions and minor cross-talk omitted for brevity)
[18:00] Liam: Quick note from an SE perspective — the perf run will try two model variants: an FP16 open model and a 4-bit quant variant. We'll measure latency, throughput, and top-k sampling quality.
[18:12] Priya: How will you measure quality regressions? Do you have tooling?
[18:16] Liam: We use prompt sets and automated evals; we'll run the NLG evals and show differences. Diego will set up regression alerts tied to those evals.
[18:26] Diego: Yep, we'll set a baseline and then alert if regression beyond agreed threshold.
[18:30] Priya: Ok. Anything else on legal/procurement?
[18:34] Ravi: Our procurement team will need a preliminary quote and contract template to review alongside security docs.
[18:40] Maya: I'll loop in the sales ops team.
[18:44] Ellen: Timeline review: send security packet by Monday, staging access by Wed, perf deep-dive next Thursday.
[18:51] Maya: That matches our notes.
[18:55] Sam: For the staging access we will open a peering request. Expect a contact from Sam O.
[19:02] (wrap-up)
[19:10] Maya: Recap: I'll send the security packet and runbook; Liam will propose benchmark plan and dates; Diego will follow up with the onboarding checklist and proposed cadence. Bluehex provides network creds and prompt set.
[19:25] Priya: Thanks everyone. We'll aim to get the access info by Tuesday EOD.
[19:30] Maya: Great. Thanks all.

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcription had several mis-heard terms ("KV cash" instead of KV cache, some speaker swaps). Final meeting minutes are captured in the summary and action items above.
